answer: One workable design: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because knoll only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, ember is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any copper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
